events.summary: First-cut entry for Casimiroa edulis drawing primarily on UF/IFAS (HS304, EENY-008), Kew POWO, PROSEA, PFAF, and the University of Arizona Campus Arboretum. Confidence is high on origin, toxicity, Giant Swallowtail host status, size, and seasonality. Lower confidence on precise Florida bloom-month window and on whether any UF/IFAS invasive assessment entry exists for this species (none found, so flagged false).

events.feedback:
To turn this White sapote profile into another narrative triumph that will make institutional writers jealous, you have some absolute gold mines in the raw data. Right now, the pieces are there, but they are scattered across "Quick Hits" and "More Information."

Here is how to weave them into a seamless, high-impact story while checking all your backend database boxes (the Yellow edibility/toxicity flags).

1. Lead with the Indigenous Revolutionary (The Genus Name)
The Critique: Right now, the fact that Casimiroa honors an Otomi freedom fighter who died in Mexico’s war of independence is buried in a bullet point. This is incredibly rare in botanical naming, which is usually dominated by wealthy European colonial botanists.

The Fix: Pull this into the spotlight right away or use it as a massive headline hook. It sets an immediate tone that this park tells deeper, more human stories than a standard municipal garden.

2. Weave the "Jekyll & Hyde" Toxicity/Edibility Narrative
The Critique
